findings: RED (file-level) — ChatMessageContentRememberTest.kt (16 cases, 731 lines): tests are self-authored replicas of the source remember blocks, NOT the production code. The remember(...) blocks at ChatMessageContent.kt:114 (messages), :148 (staleQuestionPartKeys), :192 (reversedMessages) are re-implemented inline in the test with a counter; no production composable is invoked (only the pure helpers filterBeforeRevert / injectMetadataMarkers / computeFilteredReversedMessages / isStaleQuestionPart / isStaleRunningPart run inside the replica body). A dropped/added key dimension in ChatMessageContent.kt would NOT fail any of these tests — the KDoc claim (lines 36-38) 'a dropped/added key dimension in the source immediately fails the corresponding test' is false. Contrast with the template ChatRenderPipelineComposeTest.kt which calls the REAL rememberRenderPipeline. The counter-inside-remember mechanism itself is sound (remember bodies re-execute only on key change — proven by the 2 'does NOT recompute' negative tests at :194 and :680, and the M3 set-equality test at :396 which correctly relies on structural Map.keys equality), so the replicas are internally consistent — but they pin the test's own copy of the contract, not the source's, so the oracle's '少一维 → 渲染陈旧' blind spot is documented, not instrumented.

ChatScaffoldSaveableTest.kt:84-92 — negative control deleted and the KDoc justification is logically flawed. The pre-tap gate (assertCountEquals(1), :230) only rules out a sticky-default false positive; it does NOT rule out a vacuous emulateSaveAndRestore cycle. If the cycle is a no-op, the sheet stays visible post-restore because showSessionPicker was never reset — count=2 passes even if the flag were plain remember. The template ScrollManagerSaveableTest.kt:72-75/115-121 treats a plain-remember reset as mandatory proof the cycle ran. Practical risk is low (framework API + template proves the environment), but the test as written cannot distinguish saveable-restored from cycle-noop.

ScrollManagerEffectTest.kt:114-117 — KDoc mechanism claim '(c) new controller[0] instance (fresh remember for plain flags)' is factually wrong: plain remember() retains state across recomposition (same MutableState instances are reused), so the post-switch reset of navFabVisible/navJumping/pendingRestoreSession is done by the LaunchedEffect(sessionId) body (ScrollManager.kt:210-214), not by fresh remember slots. The assertions are still correct — deleting the effect body leaves the probed mutations in place and the test fails; the followBottom=true negative control (:150-157) genuinely pins the saveable boundary — but the documented mechanism misleads.

ScrollManagerEffectTest.kt:281 — mainClock.advanceTimeBy(3001) genuinely drives delay(3000) under Robolectric. The KDoc (:234-247) honestly documents the uncertainty. Nit: the assertion only pins 'auto-hide fires within 3001ms' — a delay(100) regression would still pass (duration not pinned tightly).

ChatScrollEffectsTest.kt — fake-green audit passed. Every re-fire test's phase-2 coVerify(atLeast=1) requires a NEW mocked call recorded after clearMocks; a dropped key dimension => no re-fire => assertion fails (genuine). clearMocks(listState, answers=false, childMocks=false) at :630 correctly preserves the totalItemsCount=5 stub so RSE phase 2's guard does not short-circuit. CVSE tests use full clearMocks(listState) safely because the non-streaming body never reads layoutInfo. The followBottom/navFabVisible assertions in USCE tests 1-3 are weak (values already at defaults) but the consumeScrollRequest coVerify is the real fire-detector. USCE Restore branch body (resolveRestoreIndex path) is not exercised.

SharedFlow timing in RSE test: MutableSharedFlow(replay=0, extraBufferCapacity=1) + tryEmit before collector subscription silently drops the value; empirically stable behind waitForIdle, but a latent flake source on loaded CI. Failure mode is loud (asserts fail), not green.
Oracle §2.2 #2 (ChatScrollEffects key tuples) — CLOSED. All 5 CVSE key dims + both restore guards; all 3 USCE dims; RSE orchestratorVM identity. Dropping any dimension fails its test.

Oracle §2.2 #3 (ScrollManager effect timing) — CLOSED for the oracle's stated P0-3 asks: session-reset fires on sessionId change + does NOT over-fire on recomposition, navFabTick 3s auto-hide with real clock advance, null-session guards, followBottom saveable boundary via negative control. Direction/bottom-track effect BODIES remain uncovered (KDoc honest: needs a live LazyColumn scroll) — acceptable per oracle's own P0-3 scope.

Oracle §2.2 #1 (ChatScaffold saveable flags) — PARTIAL. showSessionPicker slot positionality is genuinely pinned via real UI gesture + StateRestorationTester. showAgentPicker/showModelPicker/pendingWorkdirPick AND chatBodySaveableHolder positionality remain open. The KDoc scoping is honest but oracle P0-1 budgeted all 4 flags — P0-1 not fully delivered.

Oracle §2.2 #5 (ChatMessageContent remember chains) — PARTIAL. The M3 set-equality case is present and mechanically correct, and all 3 remember key tuples are pinned as documented contracts — but replica-bound: source-side drift is undetected, so this blind spot is only documented.
Oracle §2.2 #4 (§R-1 expand-key handoff) — NOT covered; correctly out of scope (explicit P1).
Net: 2 of 5 oracle blind spots fully closed (ChatScrollEffects key tuples, ScrollManager timing), 2 partially closed (ChatScaffold flags, ChatMessageContent remembers), 1 explicitly deferred (§R-1).

summary: The bundle delivers genuine regression protection for the two highest-ROI oracle blind spots — ChatScrollEffects key tuples and ScrollManager effect timing — with exemplary failure messages and mostly honest gap documentation; check.sh integration is clean. However P0 is only partially closed: ChatScaffoldSaveableTest pins 1 of 4 saveable flags and lacks the template's negative-control proof that the restore cycle actually ran, and ChatMessageContentRememberTest (16 cases, the largest file) tests self-authored replicas rather than the production remembers, so source-side key-tuple drift would not be detected despite the KDoc's claim. No blocking defects; the nits above should be addressed before the bundle is relied on as the P0-1/P0-4 defense line.
uncertain: ChatScaffoldSaveableTest vacuous-cycle: whether emulateSaveAndRestore genuinely applies restored state for THIS ChatScaffold composition is unproven by the test itself (no negative control).
ChatMessageContentRememberTest source-binding: whether a future refactor touching ChatMessageContent.kt key tuples would be noticed via code review of the stale replica — process risk.
RobolectricMainTestClock driving Handler-posted delay(3000): mechanism inferred from empirical green + framework knowledge.
